parts.text: Second-pass conference on the garage-door problem. Your previous answer identified an asymmetric high-energy jam: one lift cable is off its drum, the opposite cable remains tensioned, the door is racked, and removing a roller released the bind and caused the door to swing up. Critique and refine the proposed solution before we give the user a final plan. Focus on the exact order of operations. In particular: (1) Is clamping the tracks and shaft enough to make it safe to unload a standard torsion spring while the door is badly racked, or is there a safer intermediate support/restraint state first? (2) Should the door be brought fully down/supported and square before cable/drum synchronization, and if it cannot be moved safely while one side is energized, what is the correct neutralization order? (3) Which steps can the user safely do now without touching spring torque, drums, bottom brackets, or loaded cables? (4) What visual facts from the supplied scenario would tell us whether this is standard exposed torsion, TorqueMaster/enclosed torsion, or extension springs? (5) Produce a final practical sequence with a hard boundary between low-risk stabilization/inspection and high-risk stored-energy work. Do not merely say call a professional; explain the actual mechanism and repair logic.
